title: The forest floor is there now — and you can't see it
question: Does litter need a palette that separates it from soil, or is an invisible floor fine for now?
context_md:
Your call landed: litter falls through its own crown to the ground, and it rots at its own rate now instead of ash's. Measured on the standard 8-tree stand at frame 10,800:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| standing litter | 4,330 | **1,018** |
| within 1 row of the ground | 22% | **61%** |
| within 4 rows | 28% | **80%** |
| resting on a branch | 3,825 | 503 |
| rotted, of ~4,600 shed | 263 | **3,659** |

So it is a forest floor at equilibrium rather than a mat that grows forever.

**Panel 1 is the real render at 4x — what you would actually see.** I cannot pick the litter out of the soil, and I do not think you will either. Litter's palette is browns 88–126 and soil's covers the same range. WP-B2 flagged this as an open cosmetic question back when there was barely any floor to look at; the fix is what makes it matter.

**Panel 2 is the same world with litter painted magenta/cyan** so you can see it genuinely is there — this is a debug overlay, not a proposal.

Also done, from your two messages: the gnome runs through leaf litter as if it were nothing (, so no wade drag and no getting stuck). On the  acceptance case he went **34 → 98 cells**, all of it from the depth fix — the run-through flag itself buys 0 extra cells there, because by then litter was already out of his way. Kept anyway, since it is what you asked for and it stops this coming back if the canopy thickens. The remaining shortfall to the 200 bar is the old "foliage reaches the ground, so a tree is a hedge" problem, which bug Y already owns.

On your future-item idea: the material flag says *which materials are light enough to wade freely*, and an item would say *whether this character can*. I left the item switch unbuilt — it needs threading tuning through seven readers for a capability nothing can grant yet — but noted exactly where it goes.
